review.verdict: Correct casting (humans for people, robot for the AI) and kind tone, but the split-frame device never renders — flat solid background with no grid — and a disconnected floating badge plus a celebratory inspector pose muddy the joke; average falls below passing.
revisionNotes: Render the background as the specified left/right split (bg navy / paper cream) with blueprint grid — the still is solid navy throughout, erasing the visual divide between the 'open door' and 'high bar' halves and losing the blueprint grid texture.

The badge prop floats disconnected above and between the two people, reading as a stray shield/trophy icon rather than something the inspector is holding up; attach it to the inspector's raised hand at the same scale.
Swap the inspector's 'cheer' pose (both arms up, big smile) for one that actually shows presenting ID while stepping forward — cheer reads as celebrating, not showing credentials at a door.

Pull the inspector/bot/building cluster toward the left third and the spokesperson/dial cluster toward the right third so the split-frame composition the brief calls for is legible as two scenes, not one group of three figures.
Add a small raw-shape desk under or beside the bot so it reads as 'seated at a desk just inside the doorway' as specified, instead of standing alone in the door frame.
Palette/layout (navy blueprint, vertical split, OPEN label, buildings) is close to a recent slopper in the gallery; vary the accent treatment or split orientation to read as fresh.

warnings: "label-open" (label) was moved 0 px, 9 px to stay inside the safe area
"label-bar" (label) was moved 0 px, 9 px to stay inside the safe area

review.verdict: The dial half reads clearly, but the chatbot and desk are nearly hidden behind the inspector's legs, and both figures' outstretched arms plus a stray badge blur the split-frame into one confused scene. This blueprint layout is also heavily reused recently. Needs revision before publishing.
revisionNotes: Separate 'bot' and 'desk' from 'inspector': they share nearly the same anchor (x=0.37 vs left-third), so the chatbot is occluded by the inspector's legs. Move bot/desk to x≈0.17 and scale bot up to 0.8 so the seated chatbot reads clearly before the inspector passes it.

Inspector and spokesperson both use pose='point' with arms reaching toward each other across the mid-line, and the badge (attached to inspector's arm) ends up floating near the spokesperson. Switch inspector's pose to 'walk' and move the badge offset to sit near their own chest.
Add a visible vertical divider (line or gutter) between the two halves per the brief's 'split frame' composition so each side reads as its own beat, not one shared scene.
Once un-occluded, confirm the desk's raw-shape silhouette (surface + two legs) is still readable at scale 0.55 next to the enlarged bot.
Keep the dial as is — needle resting low-left with the yellow zone isolated at the very top reads clearly as 'barely reacts until near-max'.
This blue blueprint, split-frame-with-dial-or-figures layout has appeared in several recent pieces; vary the palette or drop the vertical split next time to avoid repetition.

warnings: "building" extends outside the safe area in the final frame (x 39…457, y 314…831)

review.verdict: Cast and concept are coherent (robot for the AI, humans for the inspector and spokesperson), but the floating disconnected badge prop, the building bleeding past the safe area, and a composition that closely echoes recent split-frame blueprint pieces drag the average below passing.
revisionNotes: Reattach the badge prop directly to the inspector's raised hand/chest (offset it close to the torso, scale ~0.6); right now it floats as a disconnected square near the divider line and reads as stray clutter, not a held badge.
Shift the building anchor left-edge inward (x from 0.23 toward 0.20, scale 0.95-1.0) to pull it back inside the safe area per the lint warning; right now it risks cropping on phone frames.

This split-frame blueprint layout (dashed vertical divider, robot on one side, pointing human on the other, tag labels top corners) is very close to at least two recent sloppers; try a single continuous scene or a different divider treatment so it doesn't read as a template repeat.
Right half feels sparse with a tall empty gap above the dial; scale the dial to ~1.0 and move the spokesperson up closer to it, or add a small plinth/stand prop to use the vertical space.

The dial's tiny top-of-arc yellow zone is the whole joke but is too subtle to read at a glance; thicken the yellow arc and consider a tiny threshold label (e.g. '$1B') so the punchline lands without a close look.
Give the inspector a slightly more neutral-to-pleasant expression walking in (current face reads mildly annoyed), since the brief frames this as the lab proudly welcoming the watchdog.
